name: Ranked dot plot
reader_question: How do items rank on one measure when the differences are small relative to the level?
relationship: Ordered comparison of single values on a shared axis that may start above zero; position, not length, carries the value.
use_when: Bars would exaggerate small differences because every value sits far from zero
The reader needs the ordering and approximate gaps, with the axis range stated
avoid_when: The measure is an additive quantity whose size relative to zero matters — use ranked-bar
Items are measured on different bases or in different units

data_contract.notes: Stated axis range; every value must fall inside it

units: One unit and basis throughout; the non-zero axis range is printed on the slide.

editable: Dots, guide lines, gridlines, tick labels and value labels as native shapes and text
not_data_bound: Dot positions are drawn on a computed scale; values are not data-bound and there is no embedded workbook
Editing a value means moving the dot and rewriting its label

table_alternative: A sorted table of item and value, with the measure and basis in the header.
variations: Two-period dots on the same rows (dumbbell)
Dots with a reference line for a stated threshold
limitations: The axis does not start at zero, so gaps must not be read as proportions
Guide lines run from the axis start and are not bars

excluded_alternatives.reason: Bar length from a non-zero baseline misstates proportions
Compresses small differences into near-identical stems
